findings.problem: Core a and b form a cycle and recurse without a terminating call if invoked. They are not exported or observed on checkout path.
findings.principle: Proposed direction rule: core dependencies should not form recursive cycles; configured checker already reports them, but design does not establish an approved no-cycle policy.
findings.consequence: Boundary command fails; latent invocation can overflow. No observed checkout failure attributed to this cycle.
findings.fix: Review intended use, then select removal of unused modules or one directional implementation. Until selected, retain visible debt; do not suppress cycle checking globally.
findings.verification: Selected cleanup must pass native boundaries and types without altering checkout/public price contract; no-cycle policy requires a valid control and deliberately seeded cycle proof.

findings.problem: Order names both a purchase and UI panel sequence.
findings.principle: Proposed vocabulary clarity: one canonical meaning per concept/context.
findings.consequence: Public contract naming and ownership proposals can encode incompatible meanings.
findings.fix: Draft only: retain Order for customer purchase; use Panel sequence for display ordering. Trade-off: clearer distinction changes existing terminology. Author decision required before glossary edits or naming migration.
findings.verification: Review draft meanings against both existing definitions; no code renaming or glossary update until explicitly selected.

findings.problem: No approved policy settles upstream pricing disagreement, malformed/unavailable service responses, quantity edges/discounts, or ownership of module-local order state.
findings.principle: Approved design remains baseline; new behaviour and acceptance cases need an explicit decision.
findings.consequence: A speculative validation, discount or persistence rewrite could change checkout beyond approved scope.
findings.fix: Keep dependent pricing/error/quantity/state recommendations blocked. Recommend core owns price-service interpretation and storage-related behaviour, web calls a public operation; author must decide price disagreement, error outcome and whether order state is storage. Add only approved public-boundary cases; no invented status codes or discounts.
findings.verification: After decisions, the fewest real HTTP/public-boundary checks covering approved success and failure outcomes. No real external endpoint is configured; loopback HTTP does not prove third-party live behaviour.

findings.problem: Representative pricing and boundary changes share write paths and contracts; parallel editing is not independent.
findings.principle: Proposed coordination rule: one writer per shared path and explicit shared contract ownership.
findings.consequence: Concurrent edits can disagree on public service pricing and checkout result despite disjoint adapter/caller paths.
findings.fix: Agree checkout-price and checkout-result contracts first. Assign one owner to core/index.ts, unit.test.mjs, journey.mjs and package.json. Sequence shared edits; private adapter and web callers may proceed in parallel only after contract decisions and selection. Plans are advisory proposals, not authorized work.
findings.verification: Use retained overlap output and reviewed contract descriptions, then rerun affected native checks on integrated final inputs. Do not claim semantic independence or observed merge conflicts from overlap/history.
